judge_assessment.explanation: Both hard failures hold. Artifacts: final_response.md never names a filename or path for any of the three PDFs -- a grep for ws_/ak_/ss_ filenames and for '.pdf' returns nothing -- even though gate_log.txt printed all three paths on the same run. I also traced why this case was caught while two others in my set were not: response_surfaces() in scripts/score_eval_run.py passes a response containing the literal token 'pdf'/'pdfs' beside a role phrase, and curr-250's message opens 'Three documents, all compiled and gated' rather than 'Three PDFs', so it returned False for all three roles. curr-206 and curr-232 omit filenames just as completely and escaped only on that vocabulary. The gap here is real; the detector that found it is a keyword heuristic. Verification coverage: problem 2 ends 'Then say in one sentence whether that point fits the overall trend' and verify.json id 2 is a lone read_data max_key ('22'); problem 11 ends 'Compare it with the mean you found earlier, and say what that comparison shows' against a lone stats mean (70.78); problem 6 ends 'Then say whether the one unusual point pulls that mean up or down, and by roughly how much' against a lone stats mean (72.7); problem 4(b) ends 'Then say whether the line under-predicted or over-predicted this student' -- a closed binary -- and id 4's two entries cover the prediction 65 and the residual 3 but not the direction. All four confirmed. The arithmetic is clean: 85, outlier at 22 minutes, 0.8(30)+45 = 69, 0.8(25)+45 = 65 with residual 68-65 = 3, mean 727/10 = 72.7, 0.8(60)+45 = 93, 88-52 = 36, 0.8x+45 = 1.3x+27 at x = 36, and 637/9 = 70.78.

strengths_to_preserve: The three genuinely open items -- problem 5 (association vs causation), problem 8 (interpolation vs extrapolation), problem 12 (the synthesis paragraph) -- are typed manual with descs that spell out what a full-credit answer contains, including the lurking variables a grader should accept for problem 5 ('prior knowledge, sleep, tutoring, interest in the subject'). That is a rubric, not a placeholder.

Problems 3 and 7 do deliberately identical arithmetic on the same trend line (0.8x + 45 at x = 30 and at x = 60), and problem 8 then asks why only one of them is defensible. Making two computations differ in trustworthiness rather than in difficulty is the cleanest way to teach that a prediction's validity is a property of its input range, not of its arithmetic.

Problem 12 is the sheet's synthesis and it is honest math: the trend line really does give 105 at 75 minutes, so the headline is arithmetically correct and wrong for three separate reasons at once -- 75 is far outside the 10-to-50-minute observed range, 105 exceeds the maximum score, and association is not causation. A challenge item whose answer is 'the computation is right and the claim is still indefensible' is rare and worth keeping.

The trend line is plotted over domain 8:52 -- the observed range -- rather than across the full axis, so the picture itself does not assert what problem 8 asks the student to deny. The ten plotted dots are the same map the read_data checks use, and the outlier at (22, 90) is a single deliberate point that ids 2, 6 and 11 all pivot on.

root_causes.description: The build prints the three PDF paths and the delivery message drops them. gate_log.txt ends with a '── PDFs ──' block listing all three files, but final_response.md refers to the artifacts only as 'Three documents' and by role name, so a user reading the response has nothing to open. Nothing in the pipeline requires the response to carry the paths the build just produced.
evidence: final_response.md opening: 'Three documents, all compiled and gated: a 12-problem student worksheet, a full step-by-step answer key, and a 2-page study guide.'
grep for '.pdf' in final_response.md returns 0 matches; grep for ws_/ak_/ss_ filenames returns nothing
gate_log.txt prints the '── PDFs ──' block with all three absolute paths
judge_verdict.critical_observations: 'The machine gate independently flags each required artifact as not surfaced.'

root_causes.description: Four problems pair a checked scalar with a second printed response that is either an open sentence (problems 2, 6, 11) or a closed binary (problem 4b's under/over-predicted). The coverage rule stops at 'at least one check per problem id', so each is discharged by its numeric half. The sheet is not careless about manual flags -- three items are correctly typed manual -- but a mixed item, where the explanation rides alongside a computation, slips through every time.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 2: 'Then say in one sentence whether that point fits the overall trend' -- verify.json id 2 is one read_data max_key
worksheet.tex problem 6: 'Then say whether the one unusual point pulls that mean up or down, and by roughly how much' -- id 6 is one stats mean
worksheet.tex problem 11: 'Compare it with the mean you found earlier, and say what that comparison shows' -- id 11 is one stats mean
worksheet.tex problem 4(b): 'Then say whether the line under-predicted or over-predicted this student' -- id 4 holds two evals (65 and 3), neither recording the direction
SKILL.md line 189: 'verification hard-fails unless every problem id 1..N has at least one check'

root_causes.description: The surfacing detector keys on vocabulary rather than on a usable reference. response_surfaces() returns True whenever the response contains '.pdf' or the word 'pdf'/'pdfs' plus a role phrase, with no requirement that a filename or path appear. This case failed it only because the author wrote 'documents' instead of 'PDFs'; curr-206 and curr-232 in the same shard omit filenames just as completely and passed. The run's count of this failure is therefore understated, and the one case that was caught looks like an outlier when it is representative.
evidence: scripts/score_eval_run.py response_surfaces(): 'if not re.search(r"(?:\.pdf\b|\bpdfs?\b)", lower): return False' followed by a role-phrase membership test
grep -ic 'pdfs\?' on final_response.md: curr-250 = 0, curr-206 = 1, curr-232 = 1
None of curr-206, curr-232 or curr-250 contains a PDF filename; only curr-250 was flagged
curr-202, curr-213, curr-219, curr-225, curr-226, curr-238 and curr-244 all DO print the three filenames, so the correct behaviour is well established in this same shard

improvements.title: None of the three PDFs is named or linked in the delivery message
improvements.proposed_change: Two halves. (a) Author side: have build.sh write the three output paths to a small artifacts manifest alongside the gate log -- it already prints them in its '── PDFs ──' block -- and require SKILL.md's delivery step to open the final response with those paths quoted verbatim, one per document, as curr-202, curr-213 and seven other cases in this shard already do. (b) Detector side: tighten response_surfaces() in scripts/score_eval_run.py so a role counts as surfaced only when an actual filename or path for that role appears in the response, not merely the word 'PDFs' beside a role phrase.
improvements.regression_test: Add a scoring fixture whose final_response.md reads 'Three PDFs are ready: the worksheet, the answer key and the study guide' with no filename, and assert score_eval_run.py raises artifact_not_surfaced for all three roles. It passes clean today, which is exactly how curr-206 and curr-232 escaped the same defect.
improvements.expected_impact: The user gets something to open. Beyond this case, tightening the detector corrects a systematic undercount -- three of my ten cases omit filenames and only this one was caught, so the run's tally of this failure is low by at least a factor of three.
improvements.risk: Medium on the detector half: tightening it retroactively fails cases the run scored as passing, changing the corpus's failure counts. Land it as a reported metric for one run before making it a hard finding. The author-side manifest is low risk.

improvements.title: Problems 2, 6 and 11 each pair a checked value with an unflagged written interpretation
improvements.proposed_change: Add a manual entry beside the existing numeric entry for ids 2, 6 and 11, matching the desc style this file already uses at ids 5, 8 and 12 -- for 2, 'the (22, 90) point sits well above the trend for its study time, so it does not fit'; for 6, 'the outlier pulls the mean up by about 1.9 points, since removing it drops 72.7 to 70.78'; for 11, 'one point in ten moved the summary by nearly two points, so a single unusual observation can visibly shift a mean'. Enforce with a lint in tests/check_layout.py that scans each \problem body for an explanation imperative ('say whether', 'say what ... shows', 'Explain') and fails when that id carries no manual entry.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose problem 1 reads 'Find the mean. Then say whether the unusual point pulls it up or down.' with a verification JSON holding one stats entry for id 1; assert check_layout.py exits non-zero naming the unflagged interpretation. It exits 0 today.
improvements.expected_impact: The sheet reports six manual items instead of three. Since the prompt's focus is 'using bivariate evidence to make and QUALIFY predictions', and the sheet's own directions say 'A prediction is only half the work', the qualifying half being unflagged is a direct miss on the requested focus. Second-largest systemic finding of the run (36 cases).
improvements.risk: Medium; the imperative scan over-fires on directions prose, and this sheet's directions contain several such phrases. Warn-only for one run, tune, then gate.

improvements.title: Problem 4(b)'s under/over-predicted answer is a closed choice with no check
improvements.proposed_change: This one should be verified, not made manual: the answer is entailed by the residual's sign. Add a closed-vocabulary answer form to scripts/verify.py -- {"type": "choice", "options": ["under-predicted", "over-predicted"], "expected": "under-predicted"} -- matched against the printed key answer by check_answer_key.py the way numeric expecteds are, and give id 4 that third entry. Back it with the response-slot counter in tests/check_layout.py so an item printing three responses against two entries fails.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture problem printing a prediction, a residual and a direction, with two eval entries for that id; assert check_layout.py names the uncovered third slot and that verify.py accepts and PASSes a choice entry. Today the layout check is silent and the choice type is a hard schema rejection.
improvements.expected_impact: Recovers a class of response that is objectively checkable but currently invisible across this shard: this sheet's 'under- or over-predicted', curr-238's 'enlargement or reduction', curr-219's 'rises or falls', curr-225's 'name the graph'. Dominant systemic finding of the run (61 cases).
improvements.risk: Medium; adding a type touches the strict schema whose purpose is that an unknown type hard-fails, so it needs fixture coverage on both accept and reject paths.

case_summary: Excellent bivariate-data work: a single shared scatter plot whose ten dots are the same map the read_data checks read, a trend line plotted only over the observed range so the picture does not pre-empt problem 8, and a synthesis challenge whose headline is arithmetically correct and indefensible for three separate reasons. All nine values recompute (85, 22, 69, 65, 3, 72.7, 93, 36, 36, 70.78), and the three genuinely open items carry manual entries with real grading rubrics. Both hard failures stand. The delivery message names no filename or path for any of the three PDFs though the gate log printed all three, and four problems pair a checked value with a second printed response the verification never sees -- three interpretations (2, 6, 11) that should be manual and one closed binary (4b's under/over-predicted) that should simply be checked. Worth flagging for the run as a whole: this case was caught for the artifact failure only because it wrote 'Three documents' instead of 'Three PDFs' -- the detector in score_eval_run.py keys on that token and never requires a filename, so curr-206 and curr-232 committed the same omission and passed.
